question.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{E}[X].$

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}, & 0<x<1 \\ \frac{3{x}^{2}}{14}, & 1\le x<2\end{aligned}
$$

current_example.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\textrm E[X].$
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14265480/assets/4f1710dc6d1dc45834e17c48f6e8b1444186e2b0b1e77ef9ad8ea67cd1f0bdb4.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the expected value using the following formula:

$$
\textrm E[X] = \int_S x \cdot f(x) \, \textrm dx
$$

 

We compute the expected value of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{0}^{3}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{3}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}x\cdot \frac{1}{4}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{3}x\cdot (\frac{x}{2}-\frac{3}{4})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{x}{4}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{3}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-\frac{3x}{4})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{2}}{8}|}_{0}^{2}+{(\frac{{x}^{3}}{6}-\frac{3{x}^{2}}{8})|}_{2}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}+\frac{31}{24} \\  & =\frac{43}{24}\end{aligned}
$$
